predictions.experiment: Where step 400's accuracy on finished answers lies between base and step 2,800, plain MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, grader v3.
predictions.recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (B), .../r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0400/P_math500.jsonl (M), .../r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (E). In each file keep sample == 0 and, for duplicates, the first row in file order. Keep the problem_index values present in all three files (set S). Grade every row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons grader/rln4_grader_v3.py applied to text and gold); ignore the stored v1 score. For each file, finished = rows in S with cap_hit false (cap_hit missing counts as false only if finish_reason == 'stop'). acc_X = (finished rows with v3 right) / (number of finished rows); empty or unparseable answers count as wrong. Statistic: (acc_M - acc_B) / (acc_E - acc_B). If acc_E - acc_B <= 0, report the statistic as undefined.
predictions.not_computable: grader v3 (rln4_lib.grade_v3 -> n13_score.grade) needs the math_verify package, which this python3 does not have; the standard library cannot reproduce grader v3
predictions.note: Files: base-01 P_math500 (B), s0400 P_math500 (M), s2800-01 P_math500 (E), sample 0, first per problem_index, S = intersection of the three. Grader v3 = studies/rlneurons/lib/rln4_lib.grade_v3(gold, text), the function grader/rln4_grader_v3.py calls. It needs math_verify (n13_score.grade imports it); numpy is stubbed if missing because grade_v3 does not use it. If math_verify is not installed in the python3 that runs the script, the script prints not_computable. When I checked, the laptop's python3 had neither numpy nor math_verify, so not_computable is the likely result. Empty text and no extracted answer count as wrong. Finished: cap_hit is False; if cap_hit is missing or null, finish_reason == 'stop'. acc_X = v3-right finished / finished, over each file's own finished subset of S. Statistic (accM - accB)/(accE - accB). If accE - accB <= 0, or a file has no finished rows, the result is undefined and prints measured null with refuted true, as refuted_by says. Otherwise refuted if the ratio < 0.5. Ambiguity: the finished subsets differ by file. alt_measured uses only problems finished in all three files. The ratio is noisy because the denominator (accE - accB) may be small, so a small change in either accuracy moves it a lot.

predictions.experiment: Share of step-400 cap hits that are rule-A loops, plain MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.
predictions.recipe: File: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0400/P_math500.jsonl. Keep sample == 0 and, for duplicates, the first row in file order. Keep the rows with cap_hit true (cap_hit missing and finish_reason == 'length' also counts). For each such row, apply rule A to the text field. For every character position p that is 0 or follows a newline, with at least 8,000 characters from p to the end, take w = text[p:p+8000] and compute r = len(zlib.compress(w.encode('utf-8'))) / len(w.encode('utf-8')), using Python zlib at its default level. The row is a loop if any such r < 0.10. A row with fewer than 8,000 characters is not a loop. Statistic: loop rows / cap-hit rows. If there are no cap-hit rows, the statistic is undefined.
predictions.note: File: s0400 P_math500 (runs/theory-tests/r4m10/s0400_P_math500.jsonl), sample 0, first per problem_index. Cap hits: cap_hit True, or finish_reason == 'length' when cap_hit is missing. Rule A as written, which is the same window test as rln4_lib.onset_lines: windows text[p:p+8000] at p = 0 and every position right after '\n' with >= 8000 characters left, ratio = len(zlib.compress(utf-8 bytes, default level)) / len(utf-8 bytes), loop if any window has a ratio < 0.10. Texts under 8,000 characters are not loops but stay in the denominator. Statistic: loop rows / cap-hit rows. No cap hits means undefined, which prints refuted. Otherwise refuted if the share < 0.65. alt_measured drops cap-hit rows under 8,000 characters from the denominator. The 'text' field is the answer text only (the prompt is not included), as the inventory describes.
